articles.title: Why millennial motherhood can feel like rearranging chairs on the Titanic
articles.summary: Have you ever experienced the Sunday spirals, where you wake up and within a few minutes it feels like the day has already been sucked away by a whirl of responsibilities?
body: Leading questions: My wife obsessively consumes US news. She’s so stressed but can’t turn off. What should I do?

What to play | If you’ve ever fancied yourself a fighter pilot, flight sim game Ace Combat 8 has just earned a rave review from our critic Patrick Lum. The visuals and mechanics are thrilling and, perhaps more surprisingly, the plot is good too.

What to read | The Lady with the Dog by Carrie Tiffany is an illustrated novella about the importance of animals in our lives. Tiffany wrote a poignant piece about the experience that inspired the book for us this week.

What to cook | Zucchini flowers are available a little earlier than usual this year, which means you can try out Julia Busuttil Nishimura’s fusilli with zucchini and creme fraiche now. If you use rennet-free parmesan, it can be vegetarian, and the recipe only takes about 30 minutes to cook.
points: Have you ever experienced the Sunday spirals, where you wake up and within a few minutes it feels like the day has already been sucked away by a whirl of responsibilities?

articles.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s former husband says he was ‘shocked’ by death of her ex-partner
articles.summary: Ryan Anderson says he reached out to Blanchard’s father to offer support after apparent overdose death of Ken Urker. The ex-husband of Gypsy Rose Blanchard has said he was “shocked” by the recent death in Louisiana of her former partner Ken Urker – and that he would be there for Blanchard and her…
body: Ryan Anderson made those remarks during an appearance on The Sarah Fraser Show podcast on Friday, providing a noteworthy reaction to the latest chapter involving Blanchard, who achieved an unusual level of celebrity in the US after spending time imprisoned for a role in the murder of her abusive mother in Missouri.
Urker was found dead inside his Lafourche parish, Louisiana, home on Thursday on his 34th birthday in what was reported to the local sheriff’s office as an apparent drug overdose.

A Lafourche sheriff’s office report said Blanchard ’s half-brother and his wife went to Urker’s home, saw him lying unconscious through an outside window, and called authorities. Deputies reported that they then went into the home and – among other things – found syringes and a spoon “next to a brown powdery substance” in a bathroom.
Meanwhile, deputies also reported, Urker was dead in a bed next to a nightstand on which was a syringe and a handgun.

articles.title: Guests Raised a Martini to Maestro Gustavo Dudamel’s Arrival at the New York Philharmonic
articles.summary: The changing of the guard at the New York Philharmonic, the oldest of America’s “Big Five” orchestras, is always a momentous occasion for the city, all the more so when the incoming music director is among the most celebrated conductors of his generation.
body: Guests were invited to don “bold black tie” attire, surely a nod to the conductor’s gift for bringing even the most stately of halls to life. That spirit—part pomp and part party, lest we forget Dudamel helped inspire the series Mozart in the Jungle —carried through the occasion.

The evening began with Venezuelan bites, including an arepa bar, on Lincoln Center’s plaza, and ended with a more traditional three-course dinner in the hall’s Grand Promenade post-performance. Rows of chairs lined the plaza’s perimeter, facing the square’s spectacular fountain. Whether intentional or not, it felt like a knowing nod to Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl shoutout to the familiar Latin family tradition of kids asleep on chairs at the function.

articles.title: It’s the Filter’s first birthday! 25 things readers loved most this year … and if we still recommend them
articles.summary: In the course of a year, we’ve tested products ranging from instant coffees and cat toys to towels and sleep masks. These are the ones you loved most. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things. The Filter US is turning one.
body: The Filter US is turning one. Over the past year, we have cooked, cleaned, hiked and generally put our homes and bodies through a lot in pursuit of things actually worth buying. We have tested packing cubes on 14 trips, spent 63 nights testing sleep masks, recruited 84 coffee drinkers to taste instant coffee and put thousands of products through their paces (and called out ones which we don’t recommend ).

And we have gone deeper: asking a food lab to test the best non-toxic pans, blind-tasting everything from protein bars to nonalcoholic beer and getting the tea on Padma Lakshmi’s favorite kitchen tools. Across hundreds of articles, we have covered everything from a satisfyingly bouncy $1,600 organic mattress to a small but mighty $9 cleaning brush. We have found the legitimately best deals on our favorite things too.

One year in, we wanted to know which things should earn a permanent place in your homes. So we pulled the 25 items our readers have loved most since the Filter US launched – then went back to the writers who originally tested them. Did the products survive months of real life? Would our testers still recommend them to you?

articles.title: At the New York City Ballet Fall Fashion Gala, Stevie Nicks and Sarah Jessica Parker Brought Down the House
articles.summary: In the 14 years since Sarah Jessica Parker established the New York City Ballet’s Fall Fashion Gala, the benefit has raised more than $40 million, drawing the biggest names across the arts, fashion, and entertainment together in support of the world-renowned dance company.
body: “It’s about revisiting something that, in your mind’s eye, is extraordinary,” the multi-hyphenate and NYCB Board Vice Chair said of the occasion: a glittering night of collaboration between some of the most prominent designers and choreographers of our time. “You watch supremely talented people come together to offer New York City one of the great, great nights at the theater.”

Thursday night’s “extraordinary” affair raised $3.45 million for the company and began even before the curtain rose on a trio of world premieres: honorary gala chair Stevie Nicks made a rare red carpet appearance (her first since the Met Gala) alongside Parker. After effectively shutting down the step-and-repeat—Parker in a balletic, hand-painted custom tulle and ribbon gown by Simone Rocha, and Nicks in a mauve Morgane Le Fay frock and flower crown—the duo joined Matthew Broderick, Nicole Ari Parker, Julia Fox, and Olivia Rodrigo for the night’s performances in David H. Koch Theater.

body: Naturally, American designers were well represented: Malle chose a Khaite lace top; Elsesser, a draped Vaquera dress with sequined floral appliqués that had walked the Spring 2027 runway just two days earlier; and Sarofim, a suit by CFDA Chairman Thom Browne, who served as the evening’s emcee.

Open for industry appointments over the following two days, the showroom marks a first for the CFDA/ Vogue Fashion Fund: All ten of this year’s finalists have made the trip to Paris together, thanks to the generous support of Sarofim. articles.title: For Her Fashion Week Debut, Heidi Klum’s Daughter Lou Takes a Style Cue From Mom
articles.summary: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
body: It’s hardly unusual for family members to borrow from one another’s wardrobes—or, at the very least, their styling tricks. For her first Paris Fashion Week appearance, Heidi Klum’s youngest daughter, Lou, took a sartorial cue from her supermodel mom, with the pair arriving at the Vivienne Westwood spring 2027 show in coordinating peplum silhouettes and vertiginous platforms.

The matching stopped there, however. Klum stayed true to her penchant for high-impact glamour in a sculptural white blazer with sweeping, rounded lapels, its waist cinched with gold buttons before flaring into a petal-like hem. She paired it with a matching floor-skimming column skirt and inky blue stacked platform heels. Lou, meanwhile, gave the silhouette a distinctly Gen Z spin in an acid-wash pink denim top with a raw, flared waistline and asymmetric matching miniskirt, finished with a snakeskin-print shoulder bag, and floral strapped platforms.

Beauty-wise, there was another subtle echo. Both wore their hair loose—Klum’s blonde lengths tousled around her shoulders, Lou’s brunette curls left voluminous and natural—and leaned into warm, smoky makeup.
points: Heidi Klum and daughter Lou put their own spins on the peplum for a mother-daughter moment at Vivienne Westwood.
